title: The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald (not the song)
summary: Josh and Chuck open the year with a memorial note for Emily's grandmother Mary, then cover the sinking of the Great Lakes ore freighter Edmund Fitzgerald on November 10, 1975. They describe the ship's design (welded, screen bulkheads, hatch clamps), its owner Northwestern Mutual, the voyage with the Arthur M. Anderson, the storm on Lake Superior, the final radio messages, the search, the wreck site, theories about the sinking (open hatches, shoal, rogue waves, loose cargo), the expeditions, and the ship's bell now at the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum. Ends with listener mail about the IBM Selectric typewriter.
topics: Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald song

segments.title: New year opening and Mary memorial
segments.summary: Josh announces the death of Emily's grandmother Mary, the Stuff You Should Know Army general, and asks listeners to post well wishes on the Facebook page. The hosts then transition to the Edmund Fitzgerald and discuss the Gordon Lightfoot song they dislike.
topics: Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald song

segments.title: Ship background and Northwestern Mutual ownership
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the Edmund Fitzgerald was a modern Great Lakes ore carrier, not an old ocean liner, built to carry taconite pellets from the iron ore boom. It was owned by Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company and named after its president.

segments.title: Design, welding, and hatch clamps
segments.summary: The ship's dimensions, screen bulkheads between three cargo holds, its welded construction rather than riveted, its increased load ratings, and its 21 hatches with manually operated clamps are described. The Arthur M. Anderson is introduced as a near sister ship.

segments.title: Departure and the route
segments.summary: Captain Ernest McSorley is introduced, along with Peter Pulser as a former captain. The Fitzgerald leaves Superior, Wisconsin on November 9 carrying about 26,116 tons of taconite. The Anderson departs shortly after; the hosts discuss Lake Superior's weather and the Zug Island hum.

segments.title: The storm and the scenic route decision
segments.summary: A gale warning hits the lake. The ship takes a northern route and then turns toward Whitefish Bay, passing shelter points such as Michipicoten Island, exposing its side to the storm.

segments.title: Final radio messages
segments.summary: McSorley radios the Anderson reporting a lost fence rail, lost vents, a list, and running pumps, and asks for company. Later he reports lost radar and a bad list, and his final message at 7:10 pm says they are holding their own before a squall hides the ship.

segments.title: Disappearance, search, and wreck discovery
segments.summary: The Fitzgerald vanished from the Anderson's radar and view in about ten minutes. The Coast Guard had few options; the Anderson and other ships searched and found only debris. The wreck was located about seventeen miles off Whitefish Point, in two sections.

segments.title: Sinking theories, expeditions, and the bell
segments.summary: Theories are discussed: open hatches with unfastened clamps, a shoal near Caribou Island, rogue waves, and loose cargo or equipment. Expeditions in 1989, 1994 and 1995 followed, with later protections, and the ship's bell was raised and is now at the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum, replaced by a replica. Gordon Lightfoot revised his lyrics about the hatches.

segments.title: Listener mail on IBM Selectric
segments.summary: Listener Ken Wells describes modifying an IBM Selectric typewriter into a computer printer for his thesis and notes its single motor and interchangeable golf ball print heads.
